svg.title: Japan at a glance — editorial infographic
svg.desc: A static infographic on Japan: a stylized map with Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka and Nagoya; a short country profile; nominal GDP from 2015 to 2024; population composition by nationality; and places to visit.

g.text: Stylized four-island view · Okinawa suggested at lower left · not a survey map
Japan is an archipelago of more than fourteen
thousand islands in the northwest Pacific,
stretching from subarctic Hokkaido to the
Four main islands — Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu
and Shikoku — hold nearly all of its 124 million
people. A constitutional monarchy and one of
the world’s largest economies, it joins a deep
classical culture to dense, inventive urban life.
From cedar shrines and tea houses to the neon canyons of Shinjuku, Japan is a country of overlapping centuries.
Shinkansen lines stitch megacities together; mountain towns still keep festivals older than the shogunate. A weaker yen has shrunk the headline
dollar economy since 2022, even as real activity, design, and cultural influence remain globally outsized. What follows is a compact reading of land, output, and people.
$5.12 trillion in 2019. The fall from 2022 is
largely a currency story: depreciation against
the dollar cut the same activity into fewer
greenbacks. In yen terms the picture is steadier.
Even at $4.03 trillion in 2024, Japan remains
among the world’s largest economies — a
manufacturing and technology power with a
*Rank among national economies, nominal US$, mid-2020s.
Japan remains one of the most ethnically
homogeneous large societies. The small and
growing foreign-resident share is led by China,
Philippines, Brazil, Nepal, Indonesia and others.
Donut is to scale. Side bars enlarge the 2.5% so groups can be compared.
Six places that still explain the country
The capital: museums, neighborhoods, and the world’s busiest rail node.
Former imperial capital — temples, gardens, and machiya streets.
Kitchen of Japan: castle, Dotonbori, and a louder urban rhythm.
Peace Memorial Park and the “floating” torii of Itsukushima Shrine.
The sacred cone, lakeside circuit, and onsen towns below the snow line.
Volcanic wilderness, Sapporo, and powder winters in the far north.
A classic first loop runs Tokyo — Hakone/Fuji — Kyoto — Osaka, with Hiroshima as a day or overnight, and Hokkaido as a separate northern chapter.

Nominal GDP, current US$ trillions, 2015–2024: World Bank and IMF World Economic Outlook series as specified. Population composition by nationality / grouping, circa 2023–24 official estimates (Japanese 97.5%, Chinese 0.6%, Vietnamese 0.4%, South Korean 0.3%, Other 1.2%).
Map is a stylized editorial drawing, not a navigational or cadastral document. City marks are approximate. “Other” in the population panel aggregates all remaining foreign-resident nationalities.
